what_it_does: This paper tackles approximate nearest neighbor search (ANNS), a core operation in machine learning systems that finds the most similar items in a dataset. Traditional approaches bottleneck either on CPUs (limited by I/O throughput) or GPUs (limited by memory capacity). DRIM-ANN uses processing-in-memory (PIM) technology embedded in DRAM chips, specifically the UPMEM platform, to compute search results directly where the data lives rather than moving it back and forth across system interconnects.
method_in_detail: The system optimizes ANNS kernels for DRAM-PIM execution: approximation tuning reduces precision where search quality is not critical, lookup tables replace expensive squaring operations, load-balancing distributes work evenly across PIM cores, and I/O optimization minimizes data movement overhead.
